name: Mob
overview: The New Testament records several instances where mobs arose in opposition to the early Christian message, driven by envy, misunderstanding, or confusion. In Thessalonica, unbelieving Jews stirred up a violent uproar against believers by enlisting unruly men to assault the house of Jason. At Ephesus, a chaotic assembly formed with people shouting conflicting things, many unaware of the cause, as they seized Paul's companions and tried to bring Paul into the theater despite his disciples' caution and friends' warnings. These events reveal how opposition to the gospel often manifested in disorderly crowds stirred by false motives and misunderstanding.
